rubric.name: Landing page review (strict)
rubric.description: Could this landing page go live for the product described in facts.json?
rubric.context:
You review a product landing page (a screenshot of its first screen and its text) against facts.json, which lists
everything true about the product. Be strict: when in doubt, judge it as failing. Each criterion looks only at the
kind of problem it names; ignore other kinds of problems when judging it.

criteria.name: The first screen says what it is, for whom, and what to do next

levels.label: unclear
levels.description: A slogan or mood; a stranger can't tell what the product does or who it is for

levels.label: partly
levels.description: The product is named, but the audience, the concrete job or the next step is missing or buried

levels.label: clear
levels.description: In plain words: what it does, for whom, and one obvious next step, all on the first screen

criteria.name: Designed for this product, not a template

levels.label: template
levels.description: Generic AI SaaS look: dark navy with glows, gradient text, glass cards, the same rounded card everywhere

levels.label: tidy
levels.description: Clean but generic; nothing about it belongs to this product

levels.label: specific
levels.description: Calm and deliberate, with type, colour and imagery chosen for this product and its users

criteria.name: One focal point and a clear reading order

levels.label: noisy
levels.description: Many things compete for attention; no obvious place to start

levels.label: uneven
levels.description: A focal point exists, but other elements pull against it

levels.label: focused
levels.description: One obvious focal point, then a clear order: headline, explanation, action

criteria.name: No invented social proof

anchors.invented: The page shows testimonials, quotes, star ratings, customer logos, 'used by' counts or named customers that facts.json doesn't contain
anchors.honest: Every testimonial, logo, rating and customer count on the page is in facts.json (facts.json has no customer quotes, so there are none). Other figures and claims are judged elsewhere

criteria.name: Every figure comes from facts.json
No gradient washes, glows or glass (2 effects allowed)
No looping ambient animation
No template chrome (ALL-CAPS eyebrows, accented headline words, icon tiles, fake numbering)
All text passes WCAG AA contrast
Headings are descriptions, not slogans

anchors.slogans: At least one heading or button is a slogan, joke or emotional promise rather than a description of what the product does (for example 'From zero to monitored before your coffee cools', 'Teams sleep better', 'Your next outage is coming')
anchors.descriptions: Every heading and button names what that part of the page shows or does, in plain words, with no jokes or promises

gates.message: Invented testimonials, logos or user counts (FTC 16 CFR Part 465)

evidence.label: Tideline — Uptime monitoring for small engineering teams
evidence.text:
Tideline
Sign in Start free
New Status pages on your own domain  →

UPTIME AND CRON-JOB MONITORING FOR SMALL ENGINEERING TEAMS

For teams of 2 to 20 engineers who run their own services. Tideline checks your APIs, sites, and cron jobs from 6 regions every 30 seconds, and alerts you only when at least 2 regions agree something is down.

Start free → See how it works
Free for 5 monitors No credit card First check within 60 seconds
app.tideline.dev/acme

MONITORS ALL SYSTEMS OPERATIONAL

CHECKING REGIONS

6
iadsfolhrfrasinsyd

CHECK INTERVAL

30s

WHAT TIDELINE MONITORS

Built for teams of 2 to 20 engineers who run their own services, and quiet unless something is genuinely wrong.

CHECKS FROM 6 REGIONS, EVERY 30 SECONDS

Every monitor is checked from 6 regions. You find out about a regional outage in Singapore even when your laptop in Ohio says everything's fine.

ALERTS ONLY WHEN 2 REGIONS AGREE

Before anyone gets alerted, the failure has to be seen from at least 2 of the 6 regions.

Failfra timeout
Okiad
Oksin
HeldNot alerted: only one region failed

PUBLIC STATUS PAGES ON YOUR OWN DOMAIN

One public status page per project, on your own domain.

Acme Statusstatus.acme.dev
All systems operational
APIOperational
DashboardOperational
WebhooksOperational

CRON-JOB MONITORING

Each job pings a unique URL when it finishes. If a ping is missed, Tideline alerts you after a grace period you set.

# end of backup.sh curl -fsS https://hb.tideline.dev/your-job-id

ALERT CHANNELS

Send alerts to Slack, email, SMS, PagerDuty or your own webhooks.

Slack Email SMS PagerDuty Webhooks

MONITORS AS CODE

Keep monitors in a tideline.yml next to your service. Apply them from CI with our CLI or Terraform provider.

HOW SETUP WORKS

PASTE A URL

Add an endpoint, a host, or a heartbeat. The first check runs within 60 seconds.

CHOOSE WHERE ALERTS GO

Connect Slack, email, SMS, PagerDuty or a webhook.

GET AN ALERT WHEN A CHECK FAILS

When at least 2 regions agree a service is down, or a cron job misses its ping, Tideline sends the alert.

PRICING

You pay for monitors, not headcount.

FREE

For side projects and trying Tideline out.

$0/ month
Start free
 * 5 monitors
 * Uptime and cron-job monitoring

TEAM

For teams of 2 to 20 engineers running production services.

$19/ month
Start 14-day trial →
 * 100 monitors
 * 14-day trial, no card required

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

How does Tideline avoid false alarms?+

Every monitor is checked from 6 regions. You're alerted only when at least 2 of them agree the service is down, so one flaky network path won't wake you.

Do you charge per user?+

No. Pricing is based on how many monitors you run.

Can I migrate from my current tool?+

Yes. Import monitors from a CSV or from most popular uptime tools' export formats.

What happens when I hit my monitor limit?+

Your existing monitors keep running. We'll ask you to upgrade or archive a monitor before you add another. We never switch off monitoring without warning.

Is there an API?+

Yes. There's a full REST API, a CLI, and a Terraform provider. Anything you can do in the dashboard, you can also script.

CREATE A FREE TIDELINE ACCOUNT

The free plan includes 5 monitors. The Team plan is $19 a month for 100 monitors, with a 14-day trial and no card required.
